title: Form 140 (earlier 26Q): what it is and why it matters

sections.heading: What is it?
text: 26Q is the quarterly **TDS return for payments other than salary** to residents, such as contractor bills, professional fees, commission or rent. You report the TDS you deducted from each payee. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (from tax year 2026-27) the same return is called **Form 140**, and TDS on these payments is section 393 (sections 193 to 194T of the 1961 Act). Returns for quarters up to March 2026 stay 26Q, including corrections filed later.

sections.heading: Who has to file it?
text: Businesses that deduct TDS on such payments. The app shows it when your profile says you deduct TDS. You need a TAN, registered on the income-tax e-filing portal.

sections.heading: How often, and for which period?
text: Quarterly, one return per quarter of the financial year. The due date is shown on this page and in your calendar.

sections.heading: What happens if it is late or skipped?
text: A late return brings a late fee for each day, and the people you paid cannot see their TDS in their tax records until it is filed.

sections.heading: Filing it yourself vs. with a CA
text: Filing it yourself is possible with the free return preparation utility, if you have few payees. A CA helps with many payees, lower-deduction certificates or corrections.
